question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Nvidia)

calls.reasoning: Q3 FY27 guidance is $108.0B +/-2% (excludes China DC compute). Nvidia has beaten its guidance midpoint every quarter recently: +2.5% to +5.7% over the last six quarters (Q2 FY27 +5.7%: guided 91, reported 96.2), with roughly +2.5% to +8% over three years. A median beat of ~5% implies ~$113-114B. Sell-side consensus is $108.8-111.4B. Downside risk is memory/supply constraints or a slow Vera Rubin ramp; upside risk is a Rubin pull-forward giving an 8%+ beat (>$116B, about 11%). Manifold market (thin, 18 trades): <110 8%, 110-112 40%, 112-114 26%, 114-116 17%, >116 10%, broadly consistent. No Polymarket/Kalshi market found.

- Sell-side consensus: MarketBeat $108.8B; ChartMill $111.36B (Oct 2026); consensus has been revised up since August.
- Report date: trackers list Nov 17 or 18, 2026, after market close (MarketBeat, Wall Street Horizon); this is the first report after Sep 30, 2026, so it qualifies.
- Resolves off the total revenue figure in Nvidia's 8-K earnings press release, not later restatements or segment figures.
- Event window: the first quarterly release after Sep 30, 2026 (expected mid/late Nov 2026). As of Oct 28, 2026 not yet reported; the fiscal quarter itself ended about late Oct 2026.
- Downside risks: memory/HBM supply constraints, Rubin ramp timing, no China revenue. Upside risks: Rubin pull-forward, a history of beats.
- Searched for: Polymarket/Kalshi Nvidia revenue markets (none found); a thin Manifold market exists.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: $108B +/-2% guidance, 8 straight beats of +2.5% to +7.9%, consensus ~$108.8-111.4B. The one factual difference, the report date (Nov 18 trackers vs Nov 25 in the question), does not matter: both fall before the Jan 1, 2027 annulment cutoff. The remaining differences are judgment calls. Run 3 set a lower low end because supply constraints could cap the beat. The runs put the upper escape at 8-11%. I carried forward the beat-distribution reference class. I took 10% upper escape from the one-in-eight precedent of a >7.4% beat and 1% lower escape, with a median of $112.9B, a little under the full 5% beat because supply constraints could cap the upside.
